risk_reasons: The changed CI gate protects app-enforced tenant isolation for service-role SQL.
An unsound parser can silently accept cross-tenant reads or mutations.
goal: Tenant-scope auditing independently proves every tenant-table alias occurrence inside outer queries, subqueries, CTEs, LATERAL blocks, and set-operation arms, allowing #629's naturally scoped SQL without scope laundering.
non_goals: Replace the heuristic audit with a full PostgreSQL parser dependency.
Broaden OR or NOT predicate acceptance.
user_visible_behavior: Repository CI accepts naturally scoped nested SQL and rejects nested tenant-table occurrences that borrow unrelated outer or sibling scope.
Requests approval and batch reads preserve their existing results while shedding SQL shapes used only to appease the old audit.
Every repository finding carries a deterministic template/statement/arm/block/binding identity so allowlist triage cannot confuse duplicate statements, aliases, or blocks in the same file.
invariants: Every service-role tenant-table alias occurrence requires its own proof in its lexical query block.
One scoped alias cannot lend scope to another alias of the same tenant table.
Sibling or unrelated subqueries cannot lend scope to one another.
Only explicit tenant-identity correlation may inherit proven ancestor scope.
Every set-operation arm is audited independently.
Block discovery, table bindings, predicates, boolean operators, and set arms consume one shared lexical representation.
Exact allowlist entries remain full-template-and-table exceptions and are applied only after occurrence analysis.
All #629 approval and batch-view behavior and performance guarantees remain unchanged.
Allowlist count and baseline move together only after repository-wide triage.
edge_cases: A scoped outer occurrence cannot mask an unscoped nested occurrence of the same table.
A scoped alias cannot mask an unscoped second alias of the same table in one block.
A child alias that shadows a scoped ancestor alias receives no inherited proof by name alone.
A tenant predicate in one sibling subquery cannot scope another sibling.
Correlation by a non-tenant row id does not confer tenant scope.
Single-quoted and E-strings, tagged and untagged dollar-quoted strings, nested block comments, and line comments cannot contribute table or predicate evidence.
Balanced placeholders remain bind atoms, quoted identifiers remain identifiers, and ordinary function parentheses are traversed so nested scalar queries remain visible.
LATERAL children may inherit only explicit tenant-identity correlation, and data-modifying CTE bodies are audited like SELECT bodies.
A CTE name shadowing a tenant table is not mistaken for a physical tenant-table reference.
Independent scalar aggregates do not reintroduce the rejected solicitation cross product.
existing_patterns_to_follow: scripts/ci/tenant-scope-audit.ts preserves conservative OR and NOT handling.
docs/security/tenant-isolation.md prefers tightening repeatable scanner limitations over adding suppressions.
test_seams: pnpm ci:tenant-scope over every repository SQL template.
approveBatch and readLatestBatch through their existing unit and live-database suites.

rollback_plan: Revert the parser, allowlist baseline, documentation, and solicitation SQL-shape cleanup together. No migration, data repair, flag change, or deployment ordering is required.
observability: ci:tenant-scope reports the post-change entry count and every newly exposed finding.
Solicitation unit and live-database suites prove runtime behavior preservation.
